one_line: Founder of the Suryavamsi Gajapati dynasty of Odisha and devoted Routaraya of Lord Jagannath, c. 1430s–1460s CE.

appearance.age_look: Mid-40s, broad-shouldered and sturdy, with the compact strength of a seasoned warrior-king.
appearance.face: Oval face with a strong jaw, medium-brown Odia complexion, sharp nose, thick brows, a neatly trimmed black moustache with a short goatee, a small vertical sandalwood tilak on the forehead, and a default expression of calm authority with determined eyes.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair pulled back into a low warrior’s knot at the back of the head, sides smooth and controlled, with a narrow gold cloth band (simple royal headband) tied around the forehead, the knot partly visible behind.
appearance.costume: He wears a long, cream-coloured cotton angarkha-style upper garment reaching mid-thigh, with wrapped overlap tied at the right side and subtle red piping along the edges, over which sits a sleeveless, fitted, deep-maroon cloth kavacha-vest reinforced with small overlapping bronze scales stitched inside; his lower garment is a rich mustard-gold silk dhoti, pleated and wrapped in the traditional coastal Odia style, falling to the ankles with a broad red border; around his shoulders is a soft, light-ochre uttariya (shawl) with fine red and green woven motifs draped from the left shoulder across the torso; he is barefoot or in simple dark-brown leather sandals; jewellery is dignified but restrained—one medium-width gold armlet on each upper arm with a sun motif, a simple gold necklace resting on the chest, and a pair of small round gold earrings.
appearance.signature: A medium-length Odia khanda sword with a slightly broad, straight blade and a gently flared tip, housed in a plain dark-brown leather scabbard with minimal brass fittings, worn at his left hip on a simple red cloth belt so he can draw it swiftly.

ref_desc: Kapilendra Deva is a mid-40s, sturdy Odia king with a medium-brown complexion, black hair in a low knot with a gold headband, cream angarkha, deep-maroon cloth kavacha, mustard-gold dhoti, ochre uttariya, modest gold jewellery, and a khanda sword at his left hip.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of Kapilendra Deva: a mid-40s, broad-shouldered Odia warrior-king with a medium-brown complexion, oval face, strong jaw, thick brows, black moustache with short goatee, and a small vertical sandalwood tilak, his thick black hair pulled into a low knot at the back with a narrow gold cloth band around his forehead. Show him wearing a long cream-coloured cotton angarkha that overlaps and ties on the right, with subtle red piping, over a sleeveless fitted deep-maroon cloth kavacha-vest that suggests hidden bronze scales, and a rich mustard-gold silk dhoti in coastal Odia wrap style reaching the ankles with a broad red border. Drape a light-ochre uttariya shawl with fine red and green motifs from his left shoulder across his torso and behind his back. Add modest royal jewellery: a simple gold necklace, small round gold earrings, and medium-width gold armlets with sun motifs on each upper arm. Put simple dark-brown sandals or bare but clean feet consistent with temple service. At his left hip, fasten a medium-length Odia khanda sword in a dark-brown leather scabbard with minimal brass fittings on a red cloth belt, clearly visible. Use a palette of cream, deep maroon, mustard gold, red, ochre, and bronze, and present front, three-quarter, and back views with consistent hairstyle, garments, and sword placement in a clean anime aesthetic.
